structure: Part 14, Templates. Read in full at commit c2078fb (the checkout's HEAD): app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-templates.html (117 lines), create-template.html (65), view-template.html (74), delete-template.html (25); app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/dashboard-template-card.html (36) and delete-confirmation.html (31); app/data/dashboard-templates.js (349, seven seeded templates: five live animal, two germinal), dashboard-templates-testing3.js (215, five live animal templates showing identification fields) and dashboard-templates-germinal.js (100, three germinal templates); app/routes.js 6793-6851 (when a template may be made from a notification, and loading a notification into a template session), 7207-7211 (delete template summary rows), 8857-9945 (saved and seeded template lists, template ids, building and saving a template from the session with its per-party addresses, GBN-AG reference generation, species matching, seeding a notification session from a template, the template review view models, and the view, change-section, edit, discard and delete handlers), 10326-10477 (templates list render, create-template journey flags, blank answers while creating a template, create page render and post, save), 12685-12715 (save and return goes to the template review page) and 13248-13352 (every /templates route, GET /notifications/make-template and its cancel). For context only I looked at helpers those ranges call: hasJourneyUpdates, isRound2TestingSessionData and isDesignRelease21OnlySessionData (routes.js 93-95, 320-345), the template-review return helpers (555-594), getCopyAsNewSourceSnapshot (6701-6726), the review page's make-template links and delete action (6910-6970, 7050-7066), the hub's primary action while creating a template (7575-7599), buildDashboardResultsText and buildDashboardSortItems (8825-8855), dashboardData.sortItems (app/data/dashboard-notifications.js 288-293), certification-purposes.js, review-page-header.html's Actions menu, review-notification.html's Save template button and POST /review-notification (13928-13940). Pages and routes covered: GET /templates (Manage templates), GET and POST /templates/create (Enter template name), GET /templates/save, GET and POST /templates/discard, GET and POST /templates/:templateId (view template), GET /templates/:templateId/change/:section, GET /templates/:templateId/use, GET /templates/:templateId/edit, GET and POST /templates/:templateId/delete, GET /notifications/make-template and GET /notifications/make-template/cancel. All paths sit under /design-release-2.1 once version-mount prefixes them. Under /design-release-2.1 the session carries _isDesignRelease21Version, so hasJourneyUpdates is true and isRound2TestingSessionData is false: the claims describe that branch, and say so where a branch differs. Templates live only in the session. One list holds both live-animal and germinal templates.

claims.statement: Making a template from a notification finds the notification by its submitted id or its reference (or uses the notification in progress when given neither); when it cannot be found the user goes back to their dashboard.

Making a template from a notification copies every answer of that notification into a fresh template-creation session, leaving out the version flags, its status, saved templates, drafts, submitted notifications, errors, success messages and any earlier template name or id, and marks the result a draft.
claims.note: mechanism: copies a notification snapshot's session keys into the template session, skipping bookkeeping keys.

claims.statement: Making a template from a notification copies the notification's arrival date and documents along with its other answers; nothing in the make-template route clears them.
claims.note: The skip list holds no arrival date or document keys. A template saved in Design Release 2.1 still drops the arrival date (p14-043).

sessionData.storageTemperature = germinalTemperatureOptions.includes(review.storageTemperature)
    ? review.storageTemperature
    : null ... const germinalTemperatureOptions = ['Ambient', 'Chilled', 'Frozen']

claims.statement: Using a template seeds the unweaned animals answer from the template when it is a valid option for the selected species, defaults it to "No" when the species have unweaned options, and leaves it blank when they have none.

Using a template saved in Design Release 2.1 seeds each of the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination addresses from its own saved address, and leaves blank any the template left blank.
claims.quote: // Saved address by address: one left out of the template stays blank.

claims.statement: Using a template with no per-party addresses (every seeded template) copies its place of origin into the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination addresses, taking the last address line as the country when it is a known country.
claims.note: mechanism: splits a seeded address's last line off as its country.

claims.statement: Using a template seeds the CPH number, port of entry, means of transport, transport identification, transport document reference, arrival date and transit countries from the template.
claims.quote:
sessionData.cphNumber = review.cphNumber || null
  sessionData.portOfEntry = review.portOfEntry || null ... sessionData.arrivalDateAtPort = review.arrivalDateAtPort || null
  sessionData.transitCountries = Array.isArray(review.transitCountries) ? review.transitCountries : []

claims.statement: Using a template seeds the transporter's name, address (joined with commas when it is a list of lines), approval number and type, but not the transporter's country.
claims.quote:
address: Array.isArray(transporterAddress)
        ? transporterAddress.join(', ')
        : (transporterAddress || null),
      approvalNumber: review.transporter.approvalNumber || null,
      type: review.transporter.type || null

claims.statement: Using a template adds its contact address (or its place of origin when it has none) as the notification's one contact address and selects it.
claims.quote:
const contactPlace = review.contactAddress || review.placeOfOrigin ... sessionData.contactAddedAddresses = [contactAddress]
    syncContactAddressSession(sessionData, contactAddress)

claims.statement: Using a template does not seed any documents, and clears any validation errors.
claims.quote:

claims.quote: pageName: 'Delete this template?',

claims.statement: The delete template page shows a summary list with one row, "Name", holding the template's title.
claims.quote: buildDeleteSummaryRow('Name', templateName)

claims.statement: Under the summary the delete template page says "Confirm that you want to delete this template." and "This action cannot be undone."
claims.quote:
confirmText: 'Confirm that you want to delete this template.', ...

This action cannot be undone.
claims.note: The confirmation partial can show the confirm text as inset text above the summary instead (confirmAsInset); the template pages do not set it.

claims.statement: The delete template page has a red "Yes, delete" warning button that posts the deletion, and a "No, cancel" link back to the template.
claims.quote: text: "Yes, delete", classes: "govuk-button--warning" ... No, cancel

claims.statement: The delete template page's back link goes to the view template page.
claims.quote: backLink: `/templates/${template.id}`,

claims.statement: The delete template page uses the journey layout rather than the dashboard layout.
claims.quote: {% extends "layouts/journey.html" %}

claims.statement: Confirming deletion removes a template the user saved, hides a seeded template for the rest of the session, and returns to the templates list with the "<title> has been deleted." banner.
Deleting a saved template that shares an id with a seeded template makes the seeded template appear in the list again.
claims.quote: const isAvailable = (template) => !deletedIds.has(template.id) && !savedIds.has(template.id)

claims.statement: The Review your template page, while a template is being created or edited, has a delete action that goes to /templates/<id>/delete for an existing template, or to /templates/discard for a new one.
claims.quote:
? ((sessionData.editingTemplateId || sessionData.templateId)
          ? `/templates/${sessionData.editingTemplateId || sessionData.templateId}/delete`
          : '/templates/discard')

claims.statement: Discarding a template being created (/templates/discard) shows the same "Delete this template?" page, with the Name row holding the template name entered (or "this template" when none), a back link and "No, cancel" link to the review page, and a "Yes, delete" button that posts to /templates/discard.
claims.quote:
const title = String(req.session.data.templateName || '').trim() || 'this template' ... backLink: '/review-notification',
    deleteAction: '/templates/discard'

claims.statement: The discard page is only shown while a template is being created; otherwise it redirects to the templates list.

Confirming discard throws away the template being created without saving it and returns to the templates list with the banner "<template name> has been deleted.", or "Template has been deleted." when no name was entered.
claims.quote:
const title = String(req.session.data.templateName || '').trim() || 'Template'

  resetNotificationJourneySession(req.session.data)
  req.session.data.templatesSuccessMessage = `${title} has been deleted.`
